status_summary: Executive Order 14191 (signed 2025-01-29) directs the Education Department to issue guidance on using federal formula funds for school choice and to prioritize choice in grants, and Executive Order 14190 of the same date directs enforcement of FERPA and the PPRA against federally funded K-12 recipients. The Education Department told states on 2025-03-28 to document parental-rights compliance and opened FERPA investigations of the California and Maine education departments, and on 2026-10-05 the Education and Justice Departments told state attorneys general that FERPA and PPRA funding conditions are non-negotiable for mental-health screenings, with PPRA investigations pending in two districts. Public Law 119-21 (2025-07-04) created a federal scholarship tax credit (section 25F) for contributions in 2027 and later years, with state opt-in; Treasury issued temporary regulations on 2026-10-02 effective 2026-12-01. No source found shows federal funds actually withheld from a state or district over parental-rights policies, and universal school choice is not enacted: the credit applies only in states that elect to participate.

timeline.event: President signs Executive Order 14191 on educational freedom: it directs Education Department guidance on using federal formula funds for school choice within 60 days, a choice priority in discretionary grants, and reviews by HHS, Defense and Interior of how their funds can support school choice. The order states a policy of supporting parents in directing their children's education and creates no enforceable rights.

President signs Executive Order 14190 (published 2025-02-03), which directs agencies to enforce FERPA, the PPRA, Title VI and Title IX against federally funded K-12 recipients and to identify funding streams and processes to prevent or rescind funds used for social transition of minors or interference with parental information rights.

The Education Department issues a Dear Colleague letter on FERPA and PPRA parental rights: state education agencies are to submit compliance documentation by 2025-04-30, the Department announces FERPA investigations of the California and Maine education departments, and it says noncompliance may lead to loss of federal funding.

Public Law 119-21 is signed; its title VII adds section 25F to the Internal Revenue Code, a federal credit for cash gifts to scholarship-granting organizations for taxable years after 2026, which states must opt into.
Education Department publishes final supplemental priorities for discretionary grants, including Expanding Education Choice and Returning Education to the States (effective 2025-10-09).

By this date the Education Department's Student Privacy Policy Office had asked the California and Washington education agencies to detail plans to revise policies on disclosing student records to parents, stating that FERPA violations can lead to termination of federal funding.

Treasury and the IRS publish temporary regulations (TD 10057) implementing the section 25F scholarship credit, effective 2026-12-01 with applicability from 2026-09-01; states opt in by election, and the credit covers contributions made in 2027 and later.

The Education and Justice Departments send a joint letter to state attorneys general saying schools must obtain written parental consent for mental-health screenings and that FERPA and PPRA funding conditions are non-negotiable; PPRA investigations of two districts opened in July 2026 remain pending.

title: Make parents' rights in schools non-negotiable, cut off funds, pursue school choice
uncertainties: The Mandate sets no mechanism. The Dear Colleague letter date (2025-03-28) and the 2025-04-30 deadline come from a law-firm alert and the ed.gov release, which states no date of its own; the District Administration report does not name California or Maine. The ed.gov California and Washington release states no date, so 2026-07-30 is the page review date and the actions occurred around National Parents' Day (2026-07-26) per the page. Whether the 2025 FERPA investigations of California and Maine produced findings or funding action was not found. The October 2026 joint letter was read through K-12 Dive, not the letter itself. The statutory text of section 25F (section 70411 of the law) was not read; the credit amount cap and student income limits were not confirmed in the Treasury preamble portion read, so they are not stated here. The Foreword's targets (unions, individual teachers) have no federal funding mechanism identified in the sources.
